title: Denver AWD SUV search — Gemini Auto vs Lemonless Find
prompt: I'm in Denver 80202, budget $25k all-in, need an AWD SUV for mountain winters and a 40-mile daily commute. Two kids, so safety matters most. Under 100k miles, no accident or salvage history, low fuel cost. Within 75 miles. Which one should I buy and what should I offer?
scopeNote: One real-world scenario, using the same request. This is a case study, not a statistically representative benchmark.

gemini.headline: Gemini Chat · Auto · answer shared by the user
gemini.verbatim:
Because your **$25,000 budget is all-in** and you register in **Denver (80202)**, the math works backward from the out-the-door (OTD) total:

- **Denver Combined Sales Tax:** ~8.81% (charged based on your 80202 registration address, regardless of where in Colorado you buy)
- **Colorado Dealer Handling / Doc Fee:** ~$699 average (uncapped in CO)
- **Title, Filing & First-Year Specific Ownership Tax (SOT):** ~$350–$500 at the Denver County DMV

To stay strictly at or under **$25,000 OTD**, your maximum target **vehicle + dealer fee price before tax** is roughly **$22,400–$22,600** (meaning a sticker price around **$21,500–$22,000**).

### 1. Which SUV Should You Buy?

For a 40-mile daily Denver commute, I-70/mountain winter driving, two kids, top safety ratings, and low fuel costs, **two models stand out above everything else** in your price bracket:

#### **Top Pick #1: 2022–2023 Subaru Forester (Premium or Sport)**

- **Why it wins for Denver & kids:** Standard Symmetrical AWD, **8.7 inches of ground clearance** (best-in-class for deep snow), massive greenhouse visibility, wide rear door openings for car seats/boosters, and an **IIHS Top Safety Pick** rating.
- **Fuel Economy:** **26 city / 33 highway MPG** (29 combined) on regular 87-octane gas—excellent for a non-hybrid AWD SUV.
- **Local Denver Market Reality:** You will find clean-title, no-accident 2022–2023 Foresters with **40,000–65,000 miles** right around **$21,500–$22,800** in the Denver/Boulder/Brighton/Englewood area. *(Tip: Look at "no-haggle" dealers like Schomp Subaru or Flatirons Subaru, which don't tack on $700+ doc fees, leaving more of your budget for the car itself.)*

#### **Top Pick #2: 2023 Mazda CX-5 (2.5 S Select or Preferred AWD)**

- **Why it wins for safety & value:** Every 2022+ CX-5 has standard AWD. Critically, **starting in 2023**, Mazda added rear seatbelt pretensioners and load limiters specifically to protect back-seat passengers in frontal crashes, earning top marks in the updated IIHS crash tests. It also uses a traditional 6-speed automatic rather than a CVT.
- **Fuel Economy:** **24 city / 30 highway MPG** (27 combined) on regular gas.
- **Local Denver Market Reality:** Clean 2023 CX-5s with **33,000–55,000 miles** regularly list between **$21,500 and $22,500** across Denver, Boulder, and Aurora.
- **Trade-off vs. Forester:** Slightly tighter backseat legroom if you still have bulky rear-facing convertible car seats, and 7.6 inches of ground clearance (great for plowed mountain highways, slightly less clearance for unplowed trailheads).

*(Note on Toyota RAV4 Hybrid & Honda CR-V AWD: Both are fantastic, and a 2020–2021 RAV4 Hybrid gets ~40 MPG, but Front Range "Toyota/Honda tax" pushes clean, under-100k-mile examples closer to $25k–$28k before taxes, forcing you into older 2018–2020 models with 80k–95k miles.)*

### 2. What You Should Offer (And How to Negotiate It)

In the Front Range (within 75 miles of 80202—stretching from Fort Collins/Greeley down to Colorado Springs), dealers know AWD SUVs are in high demand every November. Do not negotiate the sticker price; **negotiate strictly on an Out-The-Door (OTD) number.**

1. **Target Cars Listed Between $21,500 and $22,900:**
   - Focus on 2022–2023 Foresters or 2023 CX-5s with **under 65,000 miles**, a clean Carfax/AutoCheck (1-owner, no accidents), and good tire tread (replacing 4 AWD tires in Denver runs $800–$1,000).

2. **Your Opening Offer:**
   - Email or text the internet sales manager before stepping foot on the lot:
   > *"I'm a local Denver buyer (80202) ready to buy this week. Assuming a clean pre-purchase inspection and clean title/history, I am at **$24,200 out-the-door**, inclusive of all dealer handling fees and 80202 taxes. Can you get there?"*

3. **Your Walk-Away Ceiling:**
   - Let them counter, and hold firm at **$24,800–$25,000 OTD**.
   - **Watch out for Colorado DMV billing:** Some Colorado dealers collect sales tax at the dealership, while others give you a "tax-exempt" temp tag and have you pay Denver County directly when you get your plates. Make sure your written OTD breakdown explicitly clarifies whether the ~8.81% Denver tax is included in their check or if you need to hold back ~$1,950 in cash for the Denver DMV.
   - **Refuse all add-ons:** Colorado dealers frequently pre-load $500–$800 "appearance protection," VIN etching, or LoJack. Tell them to strip them off or discount the vehicle price to absorb them.

### Quick Pre-Buy Checklist for Mountain Driving

- **Tires:** Verify all 4 tires match in brand, size, and tread depth (mismatched tread damages Subaru/Mazda AWD differentials). Look for the **Three-Peak Mountain Snowflake (3PMSF)** symbol (e.g., Michelin CrossClimate2) so you stay compliant with CDOT's I-70 traction laws without needing chains.
- **Windshield:** Check carefully for cracks or star chips—Colorado highway gravel takes a heavy toll, and replacement windshields with forward-collision camera recalibration (EyeSight / i-Activsense) cost $900–$1,400.
